persons.name: Puruṣottamāśrama
persons.evidence: svāminā śrīpuruṣottamamāśrameṇa yatināni yuktena ... tasyaiva niyoktur idaṃ pustakam; śrīsvāmīpuruṣottamaḥ aṇveṣyāviś cakāredaṃ māhātmyaṃ

relations.evidence: yatinā niyuktena ... rāmajīdāsaśarmaṇā vilikhya ... tasyaiva niyoktur idaṃ pustakam

purpose: parārtha: copied for the commissioner Svāmī Puruṣottamāśrama, who owns the book
notes: The colophon says only 'saṃvat 1938'. VS is inferred: it fits the north Indian context, and VS 1938 Bhādrapada kṛṣṇa 8 (pūrṇimānta), i.e. Janmāṣṭamī, falls around 18 Aug 1881, which was a Thursday, matching guruvāsara. The catalogue's 'ŚS 1838' (=1916 CE) does not match the colophon and is probably a cataloguing slip. Read as ŚS, 1938 would be 2016 CE, which is impossible. The verse chronogram rasa(6)-vahni(3)-aṅka(9)-candra(1), read right to left, gives 1936 (probably VS, c. 1879). This is the year Puruṣottama found and made known the 'hidden' māhātmya, two years before the copy. 'aṇveṣyāviś' stands for anviṣyāviś; 'apyuta' is unclear. 'yatināni yuktena' is read as 'yatinā niyuktena'. 'puruṣottamamāśrameṇa' is read as Puruṣottamāśrama. The colophon gives Vilāsapura only as the scribe's residence, not explicitly as the place of copying. It may be Bilaspur (Himachal Pradesh, which would suit a Himādikhaṇḍa text) or Bilaspur (Chhattisgarh), so it is left unnormalised.
